무슨.forms: 무슨 + noun: 무슨 요일 · 무슨 일 · 무슨 음식
무슨.x: What day of the week is it today?
무슨.e: 무슨 일이에요? 'What's going on?'; 무슨 요일 = 'what day of the week'.

여동생.x: My younger sister sings really well.

반찬.x: Could I have some more side dishes, please?
반찬.t: At Korean restaurants, 반찬 are usually free and refillable.

텔레비전.x: I eat dinner and watch TV.
텔레비전.e: From English 'television'; usually shortened to 티비 (TV).
텔레비전.t: In speech people often say 티브이 (TV). 'Watch TV' = 텔레비전을 보다.

샤워하다.x: I took a shower after working out.

바이올린.ex: 저는 일곱 살 때부터 바이올린을 배웠어요.
바이올린.x: I've been learning the violin since I was seven.
바이올린.e: From English 'violin'; Korean has no 'v', so it becomes ㅂ.
바이올린.t: For the violin, Koreans say 바이올린을 켜다 or simply 바이올린을 하다.

잘 부탁드립니다.forms: 잘 부탁해 (casual) · 잘 부탁해요 (polite) · 잘 부탁드립니다 (formal)
잘 부탁드립니다.m: I look forward to working with you; please treat me well
잘 부탁드립니다.x: Nice to meet you. I look forward to working with you.
잘 부탁드립니다.e: Literally 'I ask you a favor well' — asking for goodwill in a new relationship.

과거.ex: 과거는 바꿀 수 없지만 미래는 바꿀 수 있어요.
과거.x: You can't change the past, but you can change the future.

과거.m: civil service examination (Goryeo and Joseon); (homonym) the past
과거.ex: 옛날 선비들은 과거에 합격하려고 열심히 공부했어요.
과거.x: In the old days, scholars studied hard to pass the civil service exam.
과거.t: Homonym: 과거 (過去) 'the past' is far more common; context tells them apart.

그만.m: stop (doing), no more; just, without meaning to
그만.ex: 밤이 늦었으니까 이제 게임 그만하고 자세요.
그만.x: It's late, so stop playing games now and go to bed.
그만.e: Root of 그만두다 (to quit) and 그만하다 (to stop).

주민센터.ex: 저는 동네 주민센터에서 요가 수업을 들어요.
주민센터.x: I take a yoga class at the local community center.
주민센터.t: Formerly called 동사무소; you go there for official documents and cheap hobby classes.

근데.forms: casual short form of 그런데 · starts a sentence
근데.m: but; by the way (spoken form of 그런데)
근데.x: By the way, what time is tomorrow's get-together?
근데.e: Spoken contraction of 그런데 'but; by the way'.
근데.t: Very common in speech and texts, even in polite 요 sentences. In writing or formal speech, use 그런데 or 하지만.

체온.ex: 열이 나는 것 같아서 체온을 쟀어요.
체온.x: I felt like I had a fever, so I took my temperature.

위반.x: Yesterday I paid a fine for running a red light.
위반.t: Common in traffic: 신호 위반 'running a light,' 속도 위반 'speeding,' 주차 위반 'parking violation.'

전달하다.m: to deliver, to pass on, to convey
전달하다.ex: 선생님의 말씀을 반 친구들에게 잘 전달했어요.
전달하다.x: I passed the teacher's message on to my classmates.

운전면허.x: I got my driver's license last summer.
운전면허.t: 'To get a license' is 운전면허를 따다, not 받다.

알맞다.x: Write the appropriate word in the blank.
알맞다.e: Contains 맞다 'to fit, to be right': think 'fits just right'.
알맞다.t: It's an adjective, so the modifier is 알맞은, not 알맞는 — a very common mistake.

단단하다.ex: 이 의자는 나무로 만들어서 아주 단단해요.
단단하다.x: This chair is made of wood, so it's very sturdy.
단단하다.e: A doubled-syllable word, like many Korean texture words.
단단하다.t: 단단하다 is usually positive (solid, firm); 딱딱하다 often sounds negative (hard, stiff).

검토하다.m: to review, to examine, to look over

소유.x: This building is owned by the city.

처리.x: Please tell me how to dispose of the trash.
처리.e: Literally 'deal with and put in order.'
처리.t: It also covers data: 데이터 처리 means data processing.

근거.x: That claim has no scientific basis.

개념.x: This concept was hard to understand at first.
개념.t: Slang: 개념 없다 means someone has no common sense or manners.

고열.x: My child suffered from a high fever all last night.

성형 수술.ex: 그 배우는 성형 수술을 받았다는 소문이 있어요.
성형 수술.x: There's a rumor that the actor had plastic surgery.
성형 수술.t: Surgery is something you receive: 성형 수술을 받다 means 'to get plastic surgery'.

수학여행.x: In my junior year of high school, we went on a school trip to Gyeongju.
수학여행.e: Literally 'study travel' — this 수학 is not the 'math' 수학.
수학여행.t: Pronounced [수항녀행] — an ㄴ is added before 여.

기억력.ex: 할머니는 연세가 많으신데도 기억력이 정말 좋으세요.
기억력.x: Even though my grandmother is quite old, her memory is really good.
기억력.t: Pronounced [기엉녁]: ㄱ becomes ㅇ and ㄹ becomes ㄴ.

네트워크.ex: 네트워크에 문제가 생겨서 인터넷이 안 돼요.
네트워크.x: There's a network problem, so the internet isn't working.
네트워크.e: From English 'network'; also used for people networks, like 인적 네트워크.

의심.ex: 경찰은 그 남자를 범인으로 의심하고 있어요.
의심.x: The police suspect that man of being the criminal.

헌신.ex: 부모님의 헌신 덕분에 대학에서 공부할 수 있었어요.
헌신.x: Thanks to my parents' devotion, I was able to study in college.
헌신.e: Literally 'offering one's body,' that is, giving oneself.

불과.forms: 불과 + number (불과 3일 만에); cf. N에 불과하다 'to be nothing more than N'
불과.ex: 그는 불과 일 년 만에 한국어를 잘하게 되었어요.
불과.x: He got good at Korean in just one year.

새삼.m: anew, afresh; all over again, now (as if new)
새삼.ex: 외국에 살아 보니 가족의 소중함을 새삼 느꼈어요.
새삼.x: Living abroad, I felt anew how precious my family is.
새삼.e: Base of 새삼스럽다; related to 새 'new'.

흔히.forms: 흔히 + verb: 흔히 보다, 흔히 ~라고 하다
흔히.x: Beginners commonly make this kind of mistake.

변신하다.m: to transform (oneself), to make over, to reinvent oneself
변신하다.ex: 그 가수는 이번 드라마에서 배우로 변신했어요.
변신하다.x: That singer transformed into an actor in this drama.
변신하다.e: Literally 'change body'; used for superheroes and image makeovers alike.

따돌리다.m: to leave out, to ostracize; to shake off, to get away from
따돌리다.x: Leaving a friend out is a bad thing to do.
따돌리다.e: The noun 따돌림 'ostracism' and slang 왕따 'outcast' come from this verb.

몰다.forms: 몰아요 · 몰았어요 · 몰 거예요 · 모세요 (ㄹ drops)
몰다.m: to drive (a vehicle); to herd, drive (animals); to corner, accuse (someone of)
몰다.x: My father drove a taxi for 30 years.
몰다.t: 범인으로 몰다 means to treat someone as the culprit, often unfairly.

붙잡다.m: to grab hold of; to catch; to hold (someone) back
붙잡다.ex: 떠나려는 친구를 붙잡고 조금 더 이야기했어요.
붙잡다.x: I held back my friend who was about to leave and talked a little longer.

단서.x: The police found an important clue in the case.
단서.e: Literally 'end of a thread': pull it and the story unravels.
단서.t: Homonym: a different 단서 means 'proviso', as in 단서를 달다 'to attach a condition', common in formal writing.

주거.ex: 도시의 주거 비용이 계속 오르고 있어요.
주거.x: Housing costs in the city keep rising.
주거.t: 주거 is housing as a need or category; 거주 is the act of living somewhere.

누수.x: There was a leak from the upstairs unit, so our ceiling got wet.
누수.t: In everyday speech people usually say 물이 새요 'water is leaking'.

무효.x: A contract without a signature is invalid.

트라우마.ex: 사고 이후 그는 운전에 대한 트라우마가 생겼어요.
트라우마.x: After the accident, he developed a trauma about driving.
트라우마.e: From English 'trauma'; used casually for any lingering fear left by a bad experience.
트라우마.t: Common pattern: X에 대한 트라우마가 있다 'have a trauma about X'.

자전.ex: 지구의 자전 때문에 낮과 밤이 생겨요.
자전.x: Day and night happen because of the Earth's rotation.

간여하다.m: to meddle in, to interfere in, to be involved in
간여하다.x: Don't meddle in other people's family affairs.

영락없이.x: The way he smiles is exactly like his father.
영락없이.e: Means 'exactly, without a doubt'; the Sino part doesn't help, so learn it whole.

애를 태우다.forms: 애를 태워요 · 애를 태웠어요 · 부모님 애를 태우다
애를 태우다.m: to fret anxiously; to make someone worried sick
애를 태우다.ex: 아이가 늦게까지 연락이 없어서 부모님이 애를 태웠어요.
애를 태우다.x: The child didn't call until late, so the parents were worried sick.
애를 태우다.e: 애 is an old word for the insides; literally 'to burn one's insides.'

알 권리.ex: 국민의 알 권리를 위해 정보를 공개해야 합니다.
알 권리.x: Information must be disclosed for the public's right to know.
알 권리.e: 알 (from 알다, to know) + 권리 (right): 'the right to know'.
알 권리.t: Pronounced [알 꿜리]: tensing after the modifier 알 and ㄴ+ㄹ becoming ㄹㄹ.

내정 간섭.ex: 정부는 그것을 명백한 내정 간섭이라고 비판했습니다.
내정 간섭.x: The government criticized it as clear interference in its internal affairs.

실세.m: real power, power broker, the person really in charge
실세.x: He is known as the real power broker in the administration.
실세.e: Literally 'real power' — not the title, but who actually decides.

보루.m: fort, stronghold; bastion, last line of defense
보루.ex: 법원은 민주주의의 마지막 보루라고 할 수 있습니다.
보루.x: The courts can be called the last bastion of democracy.
보루.e: Literally 'fort and rampart', a small fortification.
보루.t: Almost always in the phrase 최후의 보루 or 마지막 보루, 'the last bastion.'

고육지책.m: desperate measure involving self-sacrifice, painful last resort
고육지책.x: As a painful last resort, the company cut its executives' salaries.
고육지책.e: Literally 'a plan of painful flesh': hurting yourself to achieve a goal.
고육지책.t: Unlike 궁여지책, 고육지책 stresses that the measure costs you something painful.

참회.ex: 그는 지난 잘못에 대해 눈물로 참회를 했어요.
참회.x: He repented of his past wrongs in tears.
참회.e: A Buddhist term for confessing sins and repenting; now also religious or deeply moral.

원죄.ex: 기독교에서는 인간이 원죄를 안고 태어난다고 봐요.
원죄.x: Christianity holds that humans are born carrying original sin.

번민.ex: 그는 밤새 번민에 잠겨 잠을 이루지 못했습니다.
번민.x: He was lost in anguish all night and couldn't sleep.
번민.t: Literary; in conversation people say 고민.

디엔에이.x: The criminal's DNA was found at the crime scene.
디엔에이.e: The English letters 'DNA' spelled out in Hangul; often simply written DNA.

광통신.ex: 광통신 덕분에 많은 데이터를 빠르게 보낼 수 있어요.
광통신.x: Thanks to optical communication, large amounts of data can be sent quickly.
광통신.e: Literally 'light communication' — data travels as light through fiber.

운율.ex: 이 시는 같은 소리를 반복해서 운율을 만들어요.
운율.x: This poem creates rhythm by repeating the same sounds.
운율.e: Literally 'rhyme and law' — the musical pattern of a poem.
운율.t: Pronounced [우뉼]; after ㄴ or a vowel, 률 is written 율.

만시지탄.m: regret that it is too late, a belated lament
만시지탄.ex: 지금 대책을 세워도 만시지탄이라는 비판이 있어요.
만시지탄.x: Critics say that even if measures are taken now, it's too little, too late.
만시지탄.e: Literally 'a sigh over the lateness of the hour'.
만시지탄.t: Pattern: 만시지탄의 감이 있다 'it feels belated', common in editorials.
rel: fixing the barn after losing the cow

폐기하다.m: to discard, to dispose of; to abolish, to scrap (a law, plan)
폐기하다.ex: 유통 기한이 지난 식품은 모두 폐기했습니다.
폐기하다.x: We disposed of all the food past its expiration date.

설파하다.m: to expound, to preach, to argue persuasively
설파하다.x: He preached the importance of peace all his life.
설파하다.e: Literally 'speak and break through' — explaining until others are convinced.

편파.x: The crowd protested the referee's biased call.
편파.t: Mostly used before a noun or with -적: 편파 판정, 편파 방송, 편파적이다 'to be biased'.

산림파괴.x: Deforestation makes the climate crisis even more serious.
산림파괴.t: Pronounced [살림파괴]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

과분하다.m: more than one deserves, undeserved, too generous
과분하다.ex: 이렇게 큰 상은 저에게 정말 과분해요.
과분하다.x: Such a big award is really more than I deserve.
과분하다.t: A humble set phrase: 과분한 칭찬이에요 'You're too kind', when accepting praise.

균열.m: crack, fissure; rift (in a relationship or alliance)
균열.ex: 지진 후에 오래된 다리에 큰 균열이 생겼어요.
균열.x: After the earthquake, large cracks formed in the old bridge.
균열.e: Cracks like the pattern on a turtle shell; the first character normally means 'turtle'.
균열.t: Pronounced [규녈]; also figurative: 동맹에 균열이 생기다, 'a rift opens in the alliance.'
